title: The Alien Who Took Thor's Hammer
question: Why did Beta Ray Bill prove worthy of Thor's hammer?

sources.title: Marvel · Walt Simonson’s Thor reading guide
sources.excerpt: Issues 337–339 introduce Bill wielding Thor’s hammer and becoming an ally.

sources.title: Modern Masters · Walt Simonson interview, pages 47–48
sources.excerpt: Simonson designed Bill to look monstrous, describes the fiery unarmed duel and explains Bill needed the power to defend his people.

sources.title: Marvel Snap · Beta Ray Bill character spotlight
sources.excerpt: The spacecraft mistook Thor for a threat. Bill fought him, picked up the hammer, and was granted Thor’s power.

sources.title: Clixnexus · Beta Ray Bill origin and duel
sources.excerpt: Bill guards a refugee fleet, wins the duel in Skartheim, and rescues Thor from the lava.

sources.title: Marvel · Thor’s Mightiest Weapons
sources.excerpt: Bill wields the original hammer and bests Thor in unarmed combat. Odin arranges a weapon of Bill’s own, Stormbreaker.

claims.text: Bill fought Thor after his ship identified Thor as a threat, then wielded Thor’s hammer.
Beta Ray Bill was the champion protecting a fleet of Korbinite refugees.
The hammer deemed Bill worthy and gave him the power of Thor.
Odin set Thor and Bill a duel without hammers in a fiery world.
Bill won the duel and saved Thor from falling into lava.
Bill sought power he could use to protect his people.
Thor kept Mjolnir and Odin commissioned Stormbreaker for Beta Ray Bill.

notes: Walt Simonson’s original Thor (1966) #337–339, 1983–84. Full pages were not reviewed. The ship, specific poses, lava ledge and hand contact are original illustrative blocking. The rescue detail was corroborated against a secondary plot synopsis and the creator’s description of the duel.
